title: Sable and the Horizon
premise: Emrys Okonkwo, a storm chaser deep in debt to the Vane Syndicate, accepts a dying prospector's map in exchange for a promise to see what lies at its end brought home safely. The expedition uncovers a buried survey proving the Syndicate poisoned the aquifer beneath three settlements — evidence worth more than gold and dangerous enough to kill for. Hunted across the drying flats by Syndicate enforcers, Emrys must choose between selling the truth to clear her debts or delivering it to the settlements' council. She brings the expedition home, exposes the findings publicly before the dry season ends, and burns her debt with the only currency the Syndicate fears: witnesses.
about_author: Ivo Coldharbour is the pen name of a former field geologist who spent a decade mapping dry riverbeds across three continents before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who keep moving because standing still was never really an option.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Promise
chapters.summary: Emrys Okonkwo's POV. Chasing a storm front for contract footage, Emrys finds prospector Halvard Sable dying in his wrecked rig and trades water and morphine for a sealed map and a promise: bring what it finds home, tell no one what it says. His last words hint the Syndicate already wants it. Emotional beat: reluctant obligation hardening into resolve as she realizes stopping — for him, for anything — has always cost more than she could pay.

chapters.title: What the Dry Season Keeps
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, with interludes from her navigator, Toma. Following Sable's map into the sink basin, the small crew digs out a buried survey station and finds records proving the Vane Syndicate knowingly poisoned the aquifer under three settlements. Toma argues they should sell it back to the Syndicate; Emrys remembers her promise. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as the crew understands the map's value — and that someone has been following their tracks since the ridge line.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Emrys and the Syndicate enforcer Rask Vey. Ambushed at the salt crossing, the crew scatters; Emrys is captured and offered her freedom and cleared debts in exchange for the survey. Recognizing Vey as a former colleague who once chose loyalty over truth, she stalls, escapes during a dust storm using her storm-reading skills, and regroups with Toma, who has decided the promise matters more than the payout. Emotional beat: betrayal, then the fierce clarity of choosing a side.

chapters.title: Sable and the Horizon
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Racing the season's last dry winds, the crew runs the survey evidence to the settlements' council ahead of Vey's riders, broadcasting the findings on every open channel so there are too many witnesses to silence. Vey stands down rather than fire on a crowd; the Syndicate's leverage dies in daylight. Emrys pays Sable's promise in full and finally stops moving — not because running got cheaper, but because some things are worth standing still for. Emotional beat: earned rest, and identity rebuilt around kept promises instead of debts.
